output.title: Host Extensions for IP Multicasting
output.author: Steve Deering
output.summary: This RFC defines how hosts extend their IP addresses to support multicast group membership. When a host joins a multicast group, it immediately sends a Report message (with the group address as both destination and group field) to inform routers of its presence. To handle potential loss/damage of initial reports, hosts are advised to repeat such reports after short delays. The protocol supports three states: Non-Member (not in group), Delaying Member (in group with report timer running), and Idle Member (in group without timer). Key events include 'join group', 'leave group', 'query received' (for valid IGMP queries at 224.0.0.1), and 'report received'. The maximum report delay is set to 10 seconds.
output.implications: Enables efficient multicast group management by allowing hosts to dynamically inform routers of their membership. Supports scalability and fault tolerance through report repetition and state tracking, while minimizing overhead via timed reporting.
